correctness.rationale: The normal-gap convention is α=π−ω. After translating the origin inside K, the tangent-intersection curve has p>0 in its moving normal coordinate and thus winding +1; each exterior point on the locus has just the two supporting tangents, with a unique ordered gap α<π. The curve is regular since u−p′=∫₀^α sin(α−v)ρ(t+v)dv/sin α>0. Green's formula then uses ordinary area. Writing X=p n+uτ (the displayed ν is u), its determinant with X′ integrates to ∫(p²+u²−2up′), which gives (1) by substituting u=(p(t+α)−p cos α)/sin α. The harmonic cross-correlations give exactly (2) and (4); the first harmonic cancels. Parseval on p″ gives ∑m⁴q_m<∞. The weighted odd-index c recurrence telescopes from infinity because (4j²−1)q_{2j}→0, while the even-index c recurrence starts at j=1 with s₀=0. This proves both inverse formulas, absolute convergence of the tails, and recovery of R² using c₁. Perimeter and area follow from the standard support integrals. For the two displayed supports, curvature radius is at least 9 and preservation of cos 2t forces the rotation part of any congruence to be a multiple of π, so a third cosine cannot become a sine.
residual_risks: Finite checks as reported corroborate chosen instances only; the inversion is not a finite-sample or noisy-data theorem.

Section 4 of 1807.09545 explicitly links the area profile F(ω) to exterior integrals as −∫f(ω)F′(ω)dω; the odd-k extension examined in 1906.10374 instead uses decomposed angles, not the single visual-angle distribution.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The even-power overlap persists after converting the data; it is not dismissed on terminology. The inspected moment statements do not give simultaneous recovery of all odd powers from the same scalar profile.

evidence: The same-level-set-area kernel including all harmonics is explicitly prior. Adjacent harmonics couple separately in each parity after projecting onto cosine modes; the unanchored even-power homogeneous tail is proportional to (4j²−1)⁻¹, excluded by the smoothness/decay hypothesis.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The power-only sufficient condition is immediate from the old formula. The converse and constructive full inverse require different endpoints for the two recurrences, notably exclusion of the homogeneous tail rather than a parameter substitution or application of the even-mode Hurwitz moment. No stronger inspected inversion subsumes this step.

evidence: With ω=π−α and L=2πR, Proposition 4.1 and its g_k of Eq. (10) are exactly the frozen forward harmonic identity, with c_k² in that paper denoting q_k. Kurusa's inverse datum is the geometric locus at an angle, not its area.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The full scalar datum equivalently gives the distribution of exterior visual angle via superlevel areas A_K(π−ω)−area(K). Equality of full curves is a much stronger measurement, whereas writing down the forward scalar kernel does not establish its injectivity on smooth support powers.

originality.rationale: The forward series (including its dependence on powers only) is classical, in Michalska and in Hurwitz's formula as reproduced by Cufí–Gallego–Reventós. There is also earlier isolation of even powers from weighted visual-angle integrals, which the full area profile determines. The distinct supported result is the explicit inverse on admissible sequences, including recovery of the odd powers from the same scalar datum and the full equality characterization. No inspected result supplies that full inverse; a forward expression as a series does not on its own establish uniqueness or give the needed boundary conditions.
residual_risks: Older isoptic/Crofton literature may contain a full inverse phrased in visual-angle-distribution terms. Priority is not certified; no originality credit for the forwarded area kernel or for the already isolated even moments.

value.rationale: The result identifies the exact information carried by a natural scalar geometric measurement: unlike full isoptic loci it cannot resolve phases, but despite this it recovers even and odd powers, perimeter and enclosed area. The parity-dependent inverses tell a user how to reconstruct all recoverable modes and exhibit the boundary condition required for uniqueness.
residual_risks: No claim about robustness, finite-angle measurements, or recovering a unique body.
